Have an idea for a deck but have to check something first.

You can put multiple Burden the Mind on a minion.
Card Text states that they can take a action to ger rid of it and
untap.
Can the minion get rid of multiple Burden the Mind cards, or does the
No Repeat Action rule apply?

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
On Oct 23, 9:37 am, "adam.hu...@gmail.com" <adam.hu...@gmail.com>
wrote:


The rule is that a minion can take an action provided by a card only
once per turn.

Each Burden the Mind provides its own action, therefore a minion can
take each action each turn (effectively taking one action to remove a
BiM per BiM.)

So yes, a minion with three BiM can remove one and untap, remove the
next and untap (new card, new action), and remove the third in turn.

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
adam....@gmail.com wrote:
> You can put multiple Burden the Mind on a minion.
> Card Text states that they can take a action to ger rid of it and
> untap.
> Can the minion get rid of multiple Burden the Mind cards, or does the
> No Repeat Action rule apply?

There is no single "No Repeat Action" rule.

Some actions are restricted, as specified in the rulebook:

Bleeds [6.1.1]
Political actions [6.1.7]
Action cards (by name) [6.1.6]
Cards in play (by instance) [6.1.6]

The action to burn a Burned is provided by the card in play.
A minion cannot attempt that action (to burn that specific Burden) more than
once in a turn, but the minion is free to attempt to burn each one (one attempt
each).

Unfortunately, your plan will not work as you are hoping for, unless
your plan is to burn your own pool. As per another thread, using an
effect to untap the Burdened vampire is paid by the Methuselah playing
the effect. So if your plan was to Burden a vampire, then tap them,
and then use Precognizant Mobility to untap them, you would be the one
paying the pool cost.
